item.title: Rust 1.99: C-Style Variadics Are Finally Definable in Rust — I Wrote a Sum Function and Let C Code Call It
item.description: Rust 1.99.0 (released Oct 1) moves extern "C" variadics to stable: Rust can now DEFINE (not just call) C-style ... functions, with ABI matching C's va_list. Measured on stable: C code calling three Rust variadic functions — i32 sums, a C string pointer, and mixed-ABI interleaving — all verified against independently computed C expectations, zero #![feature] gates. Plus two other new stabilizations: Vec::into_parts, String::from_utf8_lossy_owned.

item.title: Stop Rewriting! The Rust FFI Sandwich: Keep Your C Code Running While You Add Safety
item.description: Rust FFI Sandwich incremental migration: stop the big-bang rewrite, wrap your C code in Rust safety layers, and migrate one function at a time while production keeps running.

item.title: Rust unsafe Done Right: 6 Common Misuses and How to Avoid Them
item.description: Rust's unsafe does not disable safety checks — it hands you the responsibility for 5 kinds of operations. Six runnable examples of common misuses: bypassing the borrow checker, dereferencing arbitrary raw pointers, violating borrow rules inside unsafe, reinventing wheels, abusing unsafe impl, and missing SAFETY comments.
